title: Earlier station weekday modes gave no clear repeated excess in later Swiss beech dates in two periods
abstract: We tested whether a station's most common earlier weekday predicts later recorded beech leaf dates. Eight tests used two phases, two Swiss regions and two periods. The analysis used 3,674 training records and 3,799 test records. No test passed a 0.05 threshold after correction for eight tests. Eastern leaf colouring in 2006-2020 had the largest positive score excess, 2.92 percentage points above 1/7, with corrected calendar-phase p = 0.0784. All eight marginal station/year bootstrap intervals included zero. No clear station-rule gain over a pooled weekday rule was found. Independent date and score checks agreed. This tests one stable calendar pattern in selected long station records. Unknown visits, changing observers, noisy training modes and dependence between years limit inference. The result does not establish absence of observation bias and does not estimate climate or pollution effects. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, checks and a figure are included.

display.caption: Held-out station weekday score excess above 1/7. Bars show marginal 95% station/year bootstrap intervals. No primary calendar-phase test passed correction for eight tests. Source: MeteoSwiss.

citations.reason: A prior US lilac weekend audit motivates a distinct test of fitted station weekday rules on later Swiss records.
Prior Swiss beech missingness audit uses overlapping source dates. We test weekday persistence and do not reuse its fitted results.
Earlier descriptive weekday-pattern work appeared in the search; our claim concerns held-out station-rule persistence.
